about: Catalogue problems settled according to upstream sources and public proof registries (scan of 28 Nov 2026): formal-conjectures main against the pinned commit, erdosproblems.com, the Palomar registry (Lean proofs whose Challenge statement and definitions match the formal-conjectures statement), VibeMathed entries resolved and independently confirmed, and Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems. Announced but unverified results (including OpenAI's openai/math release) are recorded as 'claimed' in data/status_overrides.json instead. Problems proved here (proofs/<id>.lean) are left out.

MovingSofa.ambidextrousSofaConstant_eq_r.reason: formal-conjectures now marks it research solved, linking the Palomar-registered Lean proof (vltanh/lean4-ambidextrous-sofa) that Romik's ambidextrous sofa is optimal and unique.

Green64.green_64.reason: formal-conjectures now marks Green's Problem 64 research solved, linking the Palomar-registered Lean proof (Inozemtsev, with GPT-6 Astra) that Ω(p − 2) is odd for infinitely many primes p.

Erdos623.erdos_623.reason: erdosproblems.com records Erdős Problem 623 as independent of ZFC, so the statement can be neither proved nor disproved.

Erdos173.erdos_173.reason: Lean proof registered on Palomar (plasma-ai/erdos-173) of exactly the formal-conjectures statement: in every two-colouring of the plane every triangle except possibly one equilateral one has a monochromatic congruent copy.

Erdos408.erdos_408.parts.i.reason: Lean proof registered on Palomar (plasma-ai/erdos-408) of exactly the formal-conjectures statement: f(n)/log n, for f(n) the least k with φ_k(n) = 1, has a limiting distribution.

Erdos408.erdos_408.parts.ii.reason: Lean proof registered on Palomar (plasma-ai/erdos-408) of exactly the formal-conjectures statement: f(n) has normal order α log n.

Erdos111.erdos_111.variants.erdos_conjec.reason: Lean proof registered on Palomar (tanclary/erdos-111-palomar) of exactly the formal-conjectures statement: for every ε > 0 there is a graph of chromatic number ℵ₁ with h_G(n) = O(n^(1+ε)).

Erdos1182.erdos_1182.parts.i.reason: Lean proof registered on Palomar (Liesegang/erdos-1182-lean) of the formal-conjectures statement with the answer f(n) = Θ(n^(3/2) (log n)^(1/2)); the upper bound is new and AI-produced.

LennonPittel.lennon_pittel_conjecture.reason: Lean proof registered on Palomar (bocowgill/lennon-pittel) of exactly the formal-conjectures statement: the number of stable matchings is at least ε_n times its expectation with probability tending to one.

OpenQuantumProblem23.sicPOVMs.reason: Lean 4 proof registered on Palomar (Hertaspace/sic-povm-lean, kernel-checked with only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice) of exactly the formal-conjectures statement OpenQuantumProblem23.sicPOVMs; it formalizes the Radchenko–Wheeler Stark-unit results and the Appleby–Flammia–Kopp ghost-SIC construction, so SIC-POVMs exist in every dimension.

wp-goldberg-seymour-conjecture.reason: Wikipedia's list now gives it among the problems solved since 2015 and no longer lists it as open (Chen, Jing and Zang, arXiv:1901.10316).

wp-does-every-convex-polyhedron-have-rup.reason: Answered no: the Wikipedia article records that Steininger and Yurkevich disproved it in 2025 with a convex polyhedron without Rupert's property (the noperthedron).

mo-1973.reason: Wikipedia's list now records the existence of a complex structure on S^6 among the problems solved (Levent Alpöge, 2026, with Claude; write-up also by Philip Engel) and no longer lists it as open.
